title: Canonical semilinear-system evaluation comparisons for open extension and proper/open source and target
statement:
Fix a universe $u$, schemes in universe $u$, a sequence $C:\mathbb N\to\operatorname{CommRing}$ with rings in universe $u+1$, and arbitrary ring homomorphisms $\tau_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$. Use the actual derived semilinear-system categories $\mathcal D_X$, their functors $P_f,R_f,J_j$, evaluation $E_{n,X}$ into the constant strict tower on $C_n$, and the normalized evaluation comparisons of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations]. Use the derived open adjunction $J_j\dashv P_j$ of [def-sf-semilinear-proper-open-comparisons] and the constant-tower open adjunction $J^{(n)}_j\dashv G^{(n)}_j$ of [def-cbc-strict-tower-open-extension]. Fix $n\in\mathbb N$. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, let $a_{j,n}:E_{n,U}P_j\cong G^{(n)}_jE_{n,X}$ be the specified inverse-image evaluation isomorphism. Define $b_{j,n}:J^{(n)}_jE_{n,U}\to E_{n,X}J_j$ to be the inverse mate of $a_{j,n}$ under these two open adjunctions, using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Define the open-unit-normalized evaluation comparison $e^J_{j,n}:E_{n,X}J_j\cong J^{(n)}_jE_{n,U}$ as the inverse of this invertible mate. The retained invertibility certificate is the existing one identifying localized extension by zero after evaluation with the same extension on the open and zero on its complement.

Write $e^R_{f,n}:E_{n,Y}R_f\cong R^{(n)}_fE_{n,X}$ for the isomorphism attached to the specified direct-image evaluation mate for $f:X\to Y$ from [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations]. For scheme maps $r:V\to S$, $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ with $i$ open, and $M\in\mathcal D_V$, define the source comparison by the composite
$$E_{n,T}(J_iR_rM)\xrightarrow{e^J_{i,n}(R_rM)}J^{(n)}_iE_{n,S}(R_rM)\xrightarrow{J^{(n)}_i(e^R_{r,n}(M))}J^{(n)}_iR^{(n)}_r(E_{n,V}M).$$
For maps $k:V\hookrightarrow W$, $p:W\to T$ with $k$ open, define the target comparison by
$$E_{n,T}(R_pJ_kM)\xrightarrow{e^R_{p,n}(J_kM)}R^{(n)}_pE_{n,W}(J_kM)\xrightarrow{R^{(n)}_p(e^J_{k,n}(M))}R^{(n)}_pJ^{(n)}_k(E_{n,V}M).$$
These are the specified composites, not arbitrary isomorphisms. The definitions require no properness, quasi-compactness, finite coefficients, flat transitions, bounded complexes, Cartesian square or chosen etale origin. They assert no proper/open invertibility or pasting theorem.
